question: Why did the error rate go up on 02 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: New deployment caused the error rate to spike.
why_chain: The change point coincides with a deployment that introduced a new version of the service.
The error rate increased sharply, indicating a new issue was introduced.
The error rate spike is concentrated in service search, suggesting the issue is specific to this service.

ruled_out.hypothesis: Configuration change caused the error rate to spike.
ruled_out.reason: No configuration change is mentioned in the evidence.

ruled_out.hypothesis: Increased traffic caused the error rate to spike.
ruled_out.reason: Request volume stayed about the same, and the error rate increase is not explained by more users.

ruled_out.hypothesis: Infrastructure issue caused the error rate to spike.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence points to an infrastructure issue, such as network or server capacity problems.

ruled_out.hypothesis: Data quality issue caused the error rate to spike.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence points to bad or unusual input data.

ruled_out.hypothesis: Unknown issue caused the error rate to spike.
ruled_out.reason: No other plausible explanations are ruled out.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service search rose from 0.36% to 3.66% (+914%), with a change point at 2026-03-02T14:05:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service search: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.14).
At the same time, request volume for service search stayed about the same (2520 per 5 min before, 2942 per 5 min after, +17%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service search rose (140 ms before, 252 ms after, +79%).
search: ERROR upstream search-cluster timeout after 3 retries (search, ap-south; 16 min after the change; record R013; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
search: ERROR upstream search-cluster timeout after 3 retries (search, eu-west; 18 min after the change; record R014; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
search-cluster status page: investigating degraded performance (search; 30 min after the change; record R016; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
search: ERROR upstream search-cluster timeout after 3 retries (search, us-east; 25 min after the change; record R015; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)

reasons: ✗ No deploy, config change, ticket or alert lines up with the change.
✓ 3 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
missing_data: Deploy and config-change history for the affected segment

actions.action: Investigate and fix the upstream search-cluster issue.
Monitor the upstream search-cluster for similar issues in the future.
Review and optimize the deployment process to prevent similar issues in the future.
